chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ibn al-Qaddah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever sends blessings upon me, Allah and His angels send blessings upon him, and whoever wishes, let him be scarce (with it), and whoever wishes, let him be frequent (with it).'
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for sending blessings upon the Prophet according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the divine reciprocity of Salawat, where Allah and His angels bestow blessings upon the sender, reinforcing the spiritual merit of this practice in Shia tradition. The Prophet’s phrase 'whoever wishes, let him reduce; and whoever wishes, let him increase' underscores the voluntary nature of the act, encouraging consistent devotion without imposing a rigid obligation, a nuance often discussed by scholars like al-Kulayni in the context of voluntary worship.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Ashary, from Ibn al Qaddah, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘The one who sends Salawāt upon mesaww, Allahazwj and Hisazwj Angels would Send Salawāt upon him, and the one who so desires to let him be scarce (with it), and the one who so desires let him be frequent (with it)’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Ash’ari from ibn al-Qaddah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “

The Messenger of Allah has said, ‘Whoever asks from Allah favors for me (in the form of al-Salat ), Allah grants him favors and the angels pray for him. It is up to people to perform this (noble) act very little or a great deal.’”
